what: What must be known before a decision can be made, what it blocks, and what would answer it. Nothing here is decided unilaterally.

questions.question: Which licensed odds source, if any, is available for closing lines?
questions.why: The market-anchored prior, every edge claim and every parlay price depend on a closing line. Without one, the site can publish model numbers but can never claim an edge against a price.
questions.blocks: market_prior, edge columns, parlay pricing, the 'bet' surface's entire economic claim
questions.would_be_answered_by: A written statement of which feed is licensed, or confirmation that none is, so the blank is permanent rather than pending.

questions.question: Where may arena coordinates be sourced from?
questions.why: The brief requires travel distance from a sourced arena-coordinate table. No official NBA page read so far publishes latitude/longitude.
questions.blocks: travel distance, and therefore any claim that travel affects the line
questions.would_be_answered_by: A citable table (e.g. an official NBA venue list with coordinates), or a decision to drop the travel feature.

questions.question: What settlement rule applies to a postponed or abandoned game?
questions.why: The three frozen strategies say 'settle on the official final'. A postponed game has no final, and the NBA rule set does not define a betting void. Deciding this after the fact is exactly what pre-registration is meant to prevent.
questions.blocks: any pick on a game that might be postponed
questions.would_be_answered_by: A rule written into the pre-registration files before the next slate.

questions.question: Should the origin results capture be extended past 2026-11-13?
questions.why: Every schedule-derived feature across the 11/13–11/14 seam depends on a single union of three captures. A daily refresh of one capture would remove the seam.
questions.blocks: nothing today (the union works), but it is a standing maintenance risk
questions.would_be_answered_by: A decision on which capture is the schedule of record, and a refresh step for it.

questions.question: How much player history is needed before minutes redistribution is published as a forecast?
questions.why: One slate of logs gives one observation per player; the share model is arithmetically correct and statistically meaningless at that size.
questions.blocks: publishing a redistribution forecast for any absence
questions.would_be_answered_by: A minimum-games threshold (e.g. 10 games per player) written into the pre-registration, plus captures meeting it.

questions.question: What correlation values are acceptable for parlay pricing?
questions.why: The brief asks for measured rho with the naive product printed beside it. The repository carries 9 correlations from an earlier session, none measured against a closing line.
questions.blocks: parlay prices on the gated surface
questions.would_be_answered_by: A stated estimation window and a source for the joint outcomes, or an explicit decision to publish naive products only.

questions.question: Is the UTC-5 fixed offset for ET tip times acceptable?
questions.why: Every 'sealed before tip' proof depends on converting ET to UTC. A fixed offset is wrong in daylight saving and is not published by any official page read here.
questions.blocks: the strength of the 'before tip' claim, though not the seal itself
questions.would_be_answered_by: A decision to use a named time-zone database, or acceptance of the stated assumption.

questions.question: Should the 13 unattributed injury rows be resolved or dropped?
questions.why: Their team column cannot be read from the PDF text layout. Assigning them by approximation would violate the no-inference rule.
questions.blocks: completeness of the availability column for those clubs
questions.would_be_answered_by: A better extraction pass over the PDF, or a decision to drop them with the omission published.
